_README: Industry events / semiconductor conferences that can move watchlist names via product announcements, roadmap disclosures, or competitive read-through. The morning routine (CLAUDE.md) refreshes dates and 'watch' notes via web search each run and adds newly-announced events. 'tickers' = watchlist symbols with direct or read-through exposure. 'partners' = KEY PRIVATE/NON-WATCHLIST COMPANIES whose appearances matter because a holding depends on them (e.g. Ayar Labs is Sivers' flagship CPO customer; Lightmatter is the CPO peer benchmark). ADDED 2026-08-07 after OCP APAC was missed: relevance must be checked against BOTH tickers and partners, and MAJOR EVENT SERIES HAVE REGIONAL EDITIONS (OCP runs Global + APAC + EMEA; SEMICON runs West/Taiwan/Europe/Korea) — enumerate every edition, not just the flagship. 'confidence': confirmed (dates verified) | approx (typical timing, verify) | rumored. Dates ISO YYYY-MM-DD, event-local. Not investment advice.

events.name: Rosenblatt 6th Annual Technology Summit: The Age of AI (Part II)
events.watch: Added 2026-08-05: broker-hosted virtual tech summit (Part I ran Jun 9-10; Part II is Aug 17-18). Watchlist relevance is narrow but dated and specific: **AAOI presents in a fireside chat on Tue Aug 18 at 11:00am ET, with Stefan Murry (CFO and Chief Strategy Officer)** — announced 2026-08-04. Calibrate expectations: this is a sell-side investor event, not a technical venue, so it produces commentary and guidance colour rather than product disclosure. Its value is timing — it falls 12 days after AAOI's Q2 print (Aug 6) and lands in the middle of the live FCC/Chinese-optical-transceiver-ban story that moved AAOI +17% on 08-04, so it is the first scheduled opportunity for management to be asked directly about import-ban exposure, 800G/1.6T capacity at the Pearland expansion, and CPO timing. A recording is posted to the company IR site afterwards. Re-verified 2026-08-06: AAOI's fireside chat with Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO) is confirmed for **Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET**; other confirmed participants now visible include Rambus, Arteris and Extreme Networks (none on the watchlist). The timing note sharpens: **AAOI reports Q2 TODAY (Aug 6, 4:30pm ET)**, so by Aug 18 management will have both the print and twelve more days of FCC-rule developments behind them — this is the first venue where the guide and the import-ban exposure get questioned together. 11 days out. **Re-checked 2026-08-06 midday: no change to the agenda since the morning pass — Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO) confirmed Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET, other visible participants Rambus, Arteris, Extreme Networks (none on the watchlist).** The one thing that changes between now and then is tonight: **AAOI's Q2 print lands at 4:30pm ET today**, so this fireside becomes either a victory-lap venue or a damage-control venue depending on a result that is still ~5 hours out at this cutoff. 11 days out. **Updated 2026-08-06 evening run (~17:30 BRT / 20:30 UTC) — the variable this entry has been waiting on has resolved: AAOI's Q2 printed at 4:30pm ET today and it was a beat with a large guide-up.** Revenue **$191.9M** (+86% YoY, +27% QoQ, above the $180-198M guide and the ~$190.5M consensus), **non-GAAP EPS +$0.06 against ~$0.03 consensus** — the first non-GAAP profitable quarter, versus a -$8.8M non-GAAP loss a year ago — and **Q3 guided to $255-290M revenue** (midpoint +44% QoQ) with non-GAAP net income $10.1-24.0M. Datacenter revenue **$107.7M, more than double** the year-ago $44.8M; 800G volume **more than doubled sequentially**; management says demand **outpaces production capacity through mid-2027** and guides capacity from ~200,000 units/month now to **~650,000 units/month of 800G and 1.6T by year-end**. **What this does to the Aug 18 fireside: it turns it from an adjudication venue into a follow-up venue, and sharpens what is actually still unanswered.** The print did NOT address the FCC/Chinese-transceiver import rule, China exposure, CPO, or datacenter customer concentration — none of those appear in the release — so Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO, Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET) is now the first scheduled venue where the import-ban exposure gets questioned against a printed quarter and a $1bn+ FY26 framing. The two questions the numbers themselves raise and the release does not answer: (a) **gross margin did not expand on a 27% sequential revenue increase** — GAAP 27.7% (down from 30.3% YoY) and non-GAAP 29.8%, at the low end of the 29-30% guide, with **adjusted EBITDA still slightly negative at -$0.5M**; and (b) the **share count**, which goes from 81.6M weighted-average basic in Q2 to **92.8M assumed for the Q3 EPS guide**, alongside cash building from $216.0M at YE2025 to $449.4M at Q1 to **$508.8M** now. 12 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-07 morning: agenda unchanged for the watchlist — AAOI's fireside chat with Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO) is still confirmed for Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET.** New participants now visible on the summit page since the last pass: **Arista Networks and Penguin Solutions** (Penguin on Aug 17), joining Rambus, Arteris and Extreme Networks — **none of them are on the watchlist**, so this changes the event's texture (a networking/AI-systems roster rather than a pure semis one) without changing what it adjudicates for this book. The substance of the entry is unchanged from the evening pass: the Q2 print has landed and it was a beat with a large guide-up, so this fireside is now a follow-up venue, and the four things the release did NOT address — the FCC/Chinese-transceiver import rule, China exposure, CPO, datacenter customer concentration — plus the two questions the numbers themselves raise (flat ~30% gross margin through a 27% sequential revenue increase; share count 81.6M -> 92.8M guided) are what Murry can be asked. 10 days out. **Re-checked 2026-08-07 midday against Rosenblatt's own summit page — agenda unchanged and now with the session framing attached: AAOI's fireside is Tue Aug 18, 11:00am EDT with Stefan Murry (CFO & CSO), moderated by Mike Genovese of Rosenblatt, under the 'Comm & Cloud Infrastructure' track.** What HAS changed since the morning pass is what this venue is for. The morning entry listed four things the Q2 release did not address — the FCC/Chinese-transceiver rule, China exposure, CPO, and datacenter customer concentration — and named Aug 18 as the first place they would be asked. **The 2026-08-06 earnings call answered all four**, so this fireside is no longer the disclosure venue for any of them: management said 'too early to say' on the import ban while noting onshore manufacturing is a selling point; put Chinese CPO-laser entrants 2-3 years out on 21-24 month equipment lead times; guided CPO laser/ELSFP at 55-65% gross margin ramping Q3-Q4 2027 toward 400,000 units/month by 2028; and disclosed that top-10 customers are 99% of revenue with one CATV customer at 42% and two datacenter customers at 26% and 24%. **What is left for Aug 18 is narrower and sharper**: the 32-33% near-term gross-margin checkpoint against a Q3 band guided at 29.0-30.5%; the funding path, given Q2 capex of $565.5M against $508.8M of cash and a $538.8M ATM; the $20-25M Q3 100G headwind that management ties to the memory shortage and expects to persist until memory supply recovers; and the Digicomm concentration. No watchlist company has been added or removed (Rambus, Arteris, Extreme Networks, Arista Networks, Penguin Solutions remain the visible non-watchlist roster). What is NEW this pass is not the agenda but the run-up to it: **@crux_capital_ (Gaetano, Tier 1 photonics — the source who put AAOI in this book) published "$AAOI Earnings. They Said Some Wild Stuff." on 2026-08-07 03:49 GMT, within ~12 hours of the call.** The post is **paywalled, so its specific claims are NOT readable and nothing from it is asserted here** — but the originating source publishing a post-call piece this fast, with that title, means the analyst community's read of the call is forming before the fireside rather than at it. The narrowed agenda from the midday pass stands unchanged as what is actually left for Aug 18: the 32-33% near-term gross-margin checkpoint against a Q3 band guided at 29.0-30.5%; the funding path (Q2 capex $565.5M vs $508.8M cash and a $538.8M ATM); the $20-25M Q3 100G headwind tied to the memory shortage; and the Digicomm 42% concentration. 10 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-12 end-of-day run directly against Rosenblatt's own summit page (rblt.com/tech2026) — read at source this pass, not via indexing.** Dates confirmed **Aug 17-18, 2026, virtual**. The AAOI session is unchanged and now fully specified: **Stefan Murry (CFO & Chief Strategy Officer), Tue Aug 18, 11:00-11:45am EDT, fireside chat moderated by Mike Genovese (Senior Research Analyst, Communications & Cloud Infrastructure)**, with Lindsay Savarese and Amy Grant (IR) also attached. **What is genuinely NEW this pass is the roster, and it changes what this event is for.** The page now shows **50+ participating companies**, and two of them matter directly: **NVIDIA (added to this entry's ticker list — a watchlist name now on the program)**, and **Coherent and Lumentum — AAOI's two closest optics-component peers, both presenting at the same summit**. The summit's own framing is now explicitly *'high-speed optical networking and silicon photonics'* as AI-infrastructure components, i.e. this is no longer a mixed broker event with one optics name on it; it is an optics-comparison venue. **The timing sharpens that further: Lumentum reported Q4 FY2026 on 2026-08-11 — revenue $1.01B (+109% YoY, high end of guide), non-GAAP gross margin above 50%, non-GAAP EPS $3.23, and a Q1 FY27 guide of $1.225-1.275B (midpoint ~+130% YoY) with EPS $4.05-4.35 — hitting its target operating model more than a quarter early.** So Murry will be answering the four narrowed questions carried from prior passes (the 32-33% near-term gross-margin checkpoint against a Q3 band guided at 29.0-30.5%; the funding path with Q2 capex $565.5M against $508.8M cash and a $538.8M ATM; the $20-25M Q3 100G memory-shortage headwind; and the Digicomm 42% concentration) **six days after a direct peer printed 50%+ gross margins on doubled revenue.** The margin question is the one that now has an unflattering live comparison attached to it. Also confirmed on the roster from prior passes: AMD, Arista, Cisco, Fortinet (plus the previously-logged Rambus, Arteris, Extreme Networks, Penguin Solutions) — non-watchlist. 6 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-13 morning run at source (rblt.com/tech2026) — dates confirmed Aug 17-18 (virtual, Part II; Part I ran Jun 9-10), and the AAOI session is unchanged: Stefan Murry (CFO & Chief Strategy Officer), Tue Aug 18, 11:00-11:45am EDT, moderated by Mike Genovese.** What is new this pass is that the peer names carried on this entry as *roster entries* now resolve into *named speakers*, which is what makes the optics-comparison framing concrete rather than inferred: **Lumentum is represented by Wupen Yuen (President, Cloud and Networking)**, **Lightmatter by Nicholas Harris (Founder & CEO)** — the CPO peer benchmark tracked in this file's partners list, appearing in person rather than as a logo — and **Arista by CFO Chantelle Breithaupt**; Coherent, NVIDIA and AMD remain on the roster (AMD via 1x1s). So the venue now puts the pluggable-transceiver case (Murry), the merchant-optics incumbent case (Yuen) and the CPO case (Harris) on the same two-day program. **The margin comparison this entry has been tracking is now fully loaded: both of AAOI's closest listed comparables have printed inside the last three days — Lumentum on Aug 11 ($1.01B revenue, +109% YoY, non-GAAP operating margin 36.6%, +2,160bps YoY) and Coherent on Aug 12 ($2.05B, +33.8% YoY, non-GAAP gross margin 40.2%) — against AAOI's own Q3 gross-margin band guided at 29.0-30.5%.** The four narrowed questions carried from prior passes are unchanged (the 32-33% near-term gross-margin checkpoint; the funding path, Q2 capex $565.5M against $508.8M cash and a $538.8M ATM; the $20-25M Q3 100G memory-shortage headwind; the Digicomm 42% concentration). 4 days out — the nearest dated catalyst on this calendar. **Re-verified 2026-08-12 morning run — dates unchanged (Aug 17-18, virtual), AAOI fireside with Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO) still Tue Aug 18 11:00am ET. 5 days out.** The reason to care has sharpened again since the last pass: @PhotonCap (Aug 11) reports the FCC's draft import ban on Chinese datacenter equipment/optical transceivers (announced Aug 4) **contains no definition separating company nationality from production origin** — and Zhongji Innolight, which raised ~$6.8B in Hong Kong on Jul 30, books ~61.7% of Q1-26 revenue from US customers while shipping ~0% mainland-origin US-bound (production already moved to Thailand/Singapore). So the ban's *drafting language*, not its existence, decides whether AAOI's competitive relief is real. AAOI rose ~20% intraday on the announcement. This fireside is the first scheduled venue where management can be asked about that definitional exposure alongside the Q2 print (Aug 6) and Pearland 800G/1.6T capacity. **Re-verified 2026-08-12 evening run (~17:30 BRT / 20:30 UTC) at source (rblt.com/tech2026) — dates confirmed Aug 17-18, 2026 (virtual), and the AAOI session is unchanged: Stefan Murry (CFO & Chief Strategy Officer), Tue Aug 18, 11:00am EDT, fireside chat moderated by Mike Genovese.** Two things are genuinely new this pass and both sharpen the margin question this entry has been carrying. **(1) The roster now visibly includes Lightmatter — a tracked partner in this file, not just a ticker — alongside Fabrinet, Coherent, Lumentum, AMD, Arista, Cisco, Fortinet, Ambarella, Arteris, Silvaco, Tenstorrent, Blaize and a quantum block (Quantinuum, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum).** Lightmatter's presence is the CPO peer benchmark appearing at the same venue as the pluggable-transceiver names, which is the comparison the optics complex is actually arguing about. **(2) Coherent reported FY26 Q4 TODAY (2026-08-12): revenue $2.05B, +33.8% YoY and +13.3% QoQ, non-GAAP gross margin 40.2% (GAAP 38.5%), non-GAAP EPS $1.74, with Datacenter & Communications at $1.615B versus $1.018B a year ago (+59%), and Q1 FY27 guided to $2.2-2.4B.** So by Aug 18, BOTH of AAOI's closest listed comparables will have printed inside eight days — Lumentum on Aug 11 (revenue $1.01B, +109% YoY, 50%+ non-GAAP gross margin) and Coherent today at 40.2% — against AAOI's own Q3 gross-margin band guided at 29.0-30.5%. **The four narrowed questions carried from prior passes are unchanged (the 32-33% near-term gross-margin checkpoint; the funding path, Q2 capex $565.5M against $508.8M cash and a $538.8M ATM; the $20-25M Q3 100G memory-shortage headwind; the Digicomm 42% concentration) — what changed is that the margin question now has two live peer prints sitting next to it rather than one.** 5 days out.
